sections.label: Budget 2023 parental support enhancements
sections.summary: Budget 2023 announced a $3,000 Baby Bonus Cash Gift increase, enhanced Child Development Account co-matching, and doubled paternity and infant care leave from 1 January 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: This year, at Budget 2023, Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong had announced the latest set of enhancements to strengthen our support for parents.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: They include an increase to the Baby Bonus Cash Gift by $3,000 and enhancing Government co-matching contributions to the Child Development Account for eligible children born on or after 14 February 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Wong also announced further enhancements to parental leave schemes, which include the doubling of the Government-Paid Paternity Leave and Unpaid Infant Care Leave from 1 January 2024.

sections.label: Reimbursing voluntary additional paternity leave
sections.summary: Clause 10 lets the Government reimburse employers who voluntarily grant up to two extra weeks of paternity leave beyond the mandatory two weeks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Clause 10 will allow the Government to reimburse employers who voluntarily grant additional paternity leave of up to two weeks to eligible employees on top of the current mandatory paternity leave of up to two weeks.

sections.label: Doubling Unpaid Infant Care Leave
sections.summary: Unpaid Infant Care Leave doubles to 12 days per parent per 12 months for working parents with a Singaporean child below two from 1 January 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Second, we will double the provision of Unpaid Infant Care Leave, from the current six days per parent per 12 months, to 12 days per parent per 12 months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: All working parents will be eligible for the additional Unpaid Infant Care Leave if they have a Singaporean child below the age of two years on or after 1 January 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: We hope that this increase will better support parents who require additional time to care for their children in the early years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Clause 2 of the Bill will allow for a simplified revocation process for Approved Persons in specific scenarios.

sections.label: Revocation process and benefit clarifications
sections.summary: The simplified revocation process in the CDCR applies when Approved Persons can no longer serve, such as being wound-up or dissolved.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: The simplified revocation process will be set out in the CDCR and are intended to apply in scenarios where the Approved Persons for the Approved Institutions are clearly no longer able to perform the role, such as when the Approved Person is wound-up or dissolved.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: There are also other clauses that clarify the total number of days of lost income that can be claimed by a self-employed person for childcare purposes in a calendar year, as well as to clarify the eligibility conditions and computation of benefits under the Government-Paid Paternity Benefit and discretionary reimbursements to employers under CDCA for employees employed for less than three months.

sections.label: Employers granting leave early
sections.summary: Since the February announcement, some employers voluntarily granted fathers the additional two weeks of leave before the 1 January 2024 implementation date.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Since the announcement by Deputy Prime Minister Wong in February this year, there have been employers who have voluntarily started granting fathers the additional two weeks of leave, even ahead of the implementation date of 1 January 2024.

sections.label: Falling total fertility rate
sections.summary: Besides doubled paternity and infant care leave, Baby Bonus and Child Development Account enhancements were made, yet the total fertility rate fell to 1.05 in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: In addition to the doubling of Government-Paid Paternity Leave and Unpaid Infant Care Leave, the Government has also increased the Baby Bonus Cash Gift by $3,000 and enhanced co-matching contributions to the Child Development Account.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Various Government agencies also prioritise families with children in areas, such as housing, and provide generous subsidies for childcare and education.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: However, we must acknowledge that despite the Government’s best efforts, our total fertility rate continues to fall, reaching a record low of 1.05 in 2022.

sections.label: Study on work-life balance
sections.summary: Speaker suggests MSF work with MOM on a local study of companies offering the best work-life balance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: I believe many Singaporeans will relate deeply with this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: I would, therefore, like to suggest for MSF to work with the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) to conduct a local study to examine companies that offer employees with the best work-life balance.

sections.label: Expanding flexible work benefits
sections.summary: Speaker urges MSF to consider expanding Part 3 of the Child Development Co-Savings Act for employers offering flexible work arrangements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: We can certainly do more to encourage more companies to adopt flexible work arrangements for their staff.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: I, therefore, urge MSF to consider expanding Part 3 of the Child Development Co-Savings Act to allow for employers to claim benefits if they provide good flexible work arrangements to staff with children.

sections.label: Baby Support Grant outcomes
sections.summary: The Baby Support Grant paid $3,000 per baby, with $92 million paid in its first year, but birth rates fell below 2019 levels.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Three years ago, this House debated the introduction of the Baby Support Grant (BSG), which offered an extra cash payment of $3,000 to encourage couples not to delay having children in the wake of the coronavirus pandemic and the scheme was extended to eligible babies born before 14 February 2023.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It was revealed that a total of $92 million was paid out in the first year that the scheme ran, a not insignificant sum of money.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: However, the birth rate in the years where the BSG payouts were made failed to go above the 2019 rate of 1.14% and in fact, dropped even to a record low in 2022 to 1.04%.

sections.label: Paternity leave increase
sections.summary: The Bill seeks to increase paternity leave entitlement from two to four weeks on a voluntary basis.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Working parents would thus take comfort in the amendments contained in this Bill to tweak our existing parental leave system to increase paternity leave entitlements for working fathers.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It seeks to increase the existing paternity leave entitlement from two to four weeks on a voluntary basis.

sections.label: GPPL take-up by fathers
sections.summary: MSF says just 40% of eligible fathers took full two weeks of GPPL yearly from 2018 to 2020, with median GPPL rising.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: From a reply to a Parliamentary Question previously, the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) says that just 40% of eligible fathers took the full two weeks of GPPL in each year from 2018 to 2020, with median GPPL taken increasing from 0.1 weeks to 1.2 weeks.

sections.label: Ensuring fathers not punished
sections.summary: The Government has a responsibility to ensure employers are not punishing fathers for taking parental leave.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Government has a responsibility to actively ensure that employers are not punishing fathers for taking up parental leave entitlement schemes and to see what effects this is having on our efforts to promote better support for young families and aspiring parents.

sections.label: Workplace fairness for working mothers
sections.summary: Speaker hopes upcoming workplace fairness legislation has measures so parents, especially working mothers, are not penalised or discriminated against.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But as the people of an improbable nation, I do not think that we do ourselves favours by selling ourselves short in thinking that this is an unachievable goal.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I hope that the upcoming workplace fairness legislation has specific measures to ensure that parents and in particular, working mothers do not end up being penalised and discriminated against, whether this is for employees being discriminated against for taking up the improved Government-Paid Maternity Leave (GPML) and GPPL entitlements or else for having to juggle childcare responsibilities with work.

sections.label: Students with special education needs
sections.summary: Latest data shows around 35,500 students had special education needs as of December last year, a significant group.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: With latest data indicating that around 35,500 students have special education needs as of December last year, this is a significant group, especially as it does not include children who are not of school-going age, but whose parents are still responsible for their care.

sections.label: Childcare leave flexibility at work
sections.summary: A workplace solution could be increased support and flexibility in childcare leave arrangements.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: A workplace solution could become an increase support and flexibility when it comes to childcare leave arrangements.

sections.label: Roadmap to equalise parental leave
sections.summary: Speaker asks whether the Government can work with tripartite partners on a roadmap to equalise parental leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Government work with tripartite partners to come up with a roadmap to equalise parental leave?

sections.label: Childcare sick leave per child
sections.summary: Speaker asks whether the Government will consider providing childcare sick leave on a per-child basis for all Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: If we are to be a Singapore Made for Families, will the Government consider providing childcare sick leave on a per-child basis for all Singaporeans?

sections.label: Baby Bonus cash for single unwed parents
sections.summary: Speaker hopes single unwed parents can now be provided the cash component of the Baby Bonus.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am glad we have previously amended this Act, the Child Development Co-Savings Act, to provide more support for single unwed parents, including providing the CDA component of the Baby Bonus.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I hope we can now provide them the cash component of the Baby Bonus.

sections.label: Baby Bonus cash for single unwed parents
sections.summary: The passage asks what the policy objective is of not giving the Baby Bonus cash component to single unwed parents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: What exactly is the policy objective of not providing the cash component of the Baby Bonus to single unwed parents?

sections.label: Changing outdated Baby Bonus policy
sections.summary: The passage says the outdated policy of not letting single unwed parents rent HDB flats was changed and this Baby Bonus policy should change too.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am quite sure we all agree they do not.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We have progressed and changed our outdated policy of not allowing single unwed parents to rent HDB flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It is time to also change this outdated policy of not providing single unwed parents with the cash component of the Baby Bonus.

sections.label: Equal Baby Bonus for single unwed parents
sections.summary: The passage says not giving single unwed parents the Baby Bonus cash component, Working Mother's Child Relief and Parenthood Tax Rebate is an injustice and inequality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: On the issue of the cash component of the Baby Bonus and the Working Mother’s Child Relief and Parenthood Tax Rebate, we are doing the single unwed parents an injustice, an inequality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am not asking for single unwed parents to have more; only that they have equal to what any other parent is entitled to.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I hope we can review our policy and start by providing the cash component of the Baby Bonus to single unwed parents.

sections.label: Singapore total fertility rate 2022
sections.summary: The passage states that in 2022 Singapore's total fertility rate was 1.05, the lowest it has ever been.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 2022, Singapore’s total fertility rate was 1.05, the lowest it has ever been.

sections.label: Approved persons eligibility and support
sections.summary: The passage asks about eligibility criteria, support and training for approved persons and how many approvals were suspended or revoked in three years.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With regard to approved persons, what are the eligibility criteria for approved persons, and what support or training are provided to help them meet these criteria?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the last three years, how many approved persons had their approval suspended or revoked, and why?

sections.label: Support for self-employed and gig workers
sections.summary: The passage says the amendment will give greater financial support to self-employed men and asks about support for gig workers and fathers' parental leave.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The amendment will provide greater financial support to self-employed men.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I would, however, welcome additional information on the support that exists for gig workers facing income loss due to parenting responsibilities; and whether the amendment covers gig workers, including those with casual or temporary hours and who have irregular income?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These amendments, I believe, will send a strong signal about the Government's commitment to a family-friendly Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, I note that strong gender imbalances with respect to parenting, family and household responsibilities still exist across many East Asian countries, including Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On that note, do we have current data on fathers' use of parental leave, particularly in the private sector, given that MSF reported that 84% of public sector employees eligible for paternity leave accessed this leave?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: What initiatives are in place to encourage men to utilise their paternity leave entitlements and how do we plan to address factors like company culture and social norms that may prevent fathers from taking up the leave?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: What measures are in place to encourage employers to support family-friendly environments for a healthy, respectful work-life balance?

sections.label: Paternity leave increase and equality
sections.summary: The speaker says greater equality for women needs greater equality for men at home, and asks if the paternity leave increase from two to four weeks is bold enough.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: If we want greater equality of opportunity for women, we need to provide greater equality for men at home.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: And so, Mr Speaker, while the increase in paternity leave from two to four weeks, including for self-employed workers, is a step in the right direction, one wonders: is it bold enough?

sections.label: Markers for mandatory paternity leave
sections.summary: The passage asks what markers would signal readiness to move from voluntary to a mandatory increase in paternity leave.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: What are the markers that would signal that we are ready to move from voluntary to a mandatory increase in paternity leave?

sections.label: Paternity and unpaid infant care leave
sections.summary: The passage says the Ministry does not track unpaid infant care leave use, cites residents' anecdotes, and calls for enshrining paternity and unpaid infant care use in anti-discrimination legislation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In a recent response to a Parliamentary Question from Mr Louis Ng, the Minister of Manpower said that the Ministry does not track the utilisation of unpaid infant care leave.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I have heard anecdotes from my Woodlands residents that taking any form of unpaid leave leads to an automatic zero bonus, that unpaid leave can only be taken when paid leave is exhausted, that shift workers are not allowed to take unpaid leave and so on.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: So, for this laudable move to not turn cynical, it is important that the use of paternity and unpaid infant care is enshrined in the proposed anti-discrimination legislations.

sections.label: Public Service and NTUC childcare leave
sections.summary: The passage states some Public Service Ministries grant six days of childcare leave per child below 12, capped at 10 days, and NTUC grants five days per child, capped at 15 days.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In the Public Service, there are Ministries that grant six days of childcare leave per child below 12 years old, capped to a maximum of 10 days.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I believe NTUC grants five days of childcare leave per child, capped at 15 days.

sections.label: TAFEP flexible work guidelines 2024
sections.summary: The passage states that in 2024, new TAFEP guidelines for flexible work arrangement will be released.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In 2024, new TAFEP guidelines for flexible work arrangement will be released.

sections.label: Legislating childcare leave for parents
sections.summary: The passage proposes legislating more childcare leave for parents with two or more children, with total days capped at say 10 days.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: First, legislating more childcare leave for parents with two or more children.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The total number of days can be capped, say, at 10 days, but recognising the increased childcare burden with more children, can be really important to drive consistency with the policy of encouraging two or more children.

sections.label: Childcare leave across sectors
sections.summary: Transport and warehousing workers need early care, IT and retail need later pick-ups, and healthcare and education can lead wider childcare leave.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: For example, transportation workers and warehousing workers often require care starting as early as 4.00 am, while IT and retail workers may need more flexibility for later pick-ups.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In high demand sectors like healthcare and education, the need to attract and retain employees and the high proportion of employees in the public sector afford the opportunity to drag along the rest of the industry in granting more childcare leave.

sections.label: Support for Bill amendments
sections.summary: The speaker supports the amendments in this Bill despite suggesting further enhancements and clarifications.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding my suggestions for further enhancements and clarifications, I support the amendments in this Bill.

sections.label: Paternity leave for self-employed men
sections.summary: A self-employed man can get 24 days of paternity leave, or six days a week for four weeks of lost income, for newborns from 1 January 2024.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: When his newborn arrives on or after 1 January 2024, a self-employed man can count on the Government for paternity leave of 24 days or six days a week for a four-week period of lost income.

sections.label: Private hire drivers financial hardship
sections.summary: The Institute of Policy Studies found more than six in 10 private hire car drivers would face prolonged financial hardship if they stopped working.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Institute of Policy Studies found that more than six in 10 private hire car drivers would fall into prolonged financial hardship if they had to stop working.

sections.label: Singapore old-age support ratio
sections.summary: Singapore's old-age support ratio declined to 3.8 in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Singapore's old-age support ratio declined to 3.8 in 2022.

sections.label: Women caregivers in study
sections.summary: Duke-NUS' Centre for Ageing Research and Education found women made up three in four of the 278 caregivers in their study.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Duke-NUS' Centre for Ageing Research and Education found that women made up three in four of the 278 caregivers in their study.

sections.label: Caregiving support in workplaces
sections.summary: The Bill lets the Government consider broader caregiving support, establishing it as a workplace norm and foundation for an inclusive workforce.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: More importantly, the Bill sets the stage for the Government to consider introducing a broader spectrum of caregiving support.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Establishing caregiving support as a norm in workplaces dignifies caregiving and caregivers.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It lays the foundation for an inclusive workforce and strengthens the resolve of workers to cope.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It makes for equal and empathetic workplaces and a kinder society.

sections.label: Paternity leave take-up data
sections.summary: About 40% to 50% of fathers took paid paternity leave last year, with a median of 1.2 weeks out of two.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: As recent data indicates, approximately 40% to 50% of fathers availed the entitled paid paternity leave last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The median number of weeks taken stood at 1.2 weeks out of the available two weeks.

sections.label: Cost of paternity leave
sections.summary: The passage asks the Government for its estimated annual commitment for the new paid paternity leave and benefits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: What is the Government's estimated annual commitment for these new paid paternity leave and benefits?

sections.label: Repayment period for funds
sections.summary: The passage asks what time period individuals have to repay funds recovered under clause 11.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: While clause 11 clarifies how the Government may recover funds from individuals who have been paid inappropriately, what is the time period for these individuals to make repayment?

sections.label: Weighing leave against businesses
sections.summary: The passage states more leave is not viable and that advancements must be weighed against effects on businesses and tracked.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Undeniably, appealing for more leave is not a viable solution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: As a small, competitive nation, we must weigh these advancements against its potential effects on businesses, ensuring a balanced approach.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We must vigilantly track the impact of these policies to discern whether they truly move the needle in the desired direction.

sections.label: Caregiving without career guilt
sections.summary: The passage urges stakeholders to build a common vision for families, recalling paternity leave was zero in 2006.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Employees should not be made to feel guilty or worry about their career progression because they had to take time off to care for loved ones.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I urge everyone, every stakeholder, including the Government, businesses and the people to build a common vision and make Singapore a strong Singapore that is made for families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: I still recall when I first entered the Chambers in 2006, paternity leave was zero.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: I am glad that we have made lots of progress since.

sections.label: CDCA paternity leave doubled
sections.summary: Key CDCA amendments include doubling paternity leave from two to four weeks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Key amendments to the CDCA, among them, a decision to double paternity leave from two to four weeks.

sections.label: Disability prevalence in population
sections.summary: Disability is estimated to affect 3% of the population.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Disability is estimated to affect 3% of our population.

sections.label: ATF cap and limited access
sections.summary: The ATF's S$40,000 lifetime cap addresses ongoing costs, but access to ATF is very limited.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While the ATF’s lifetime cap of S$40,000 seeks to account for ongoing costs that could stray well into the tens of thousands, access to ATF is very limited.

sections.label: Median household income 2022
sections.summary: Singstat reports median per capita household monthly income from work rose to almost S$3,300 in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to Singstat, median per capita household monthly income from work has risen to almost S$3,300 in 2022.

sections.label: Support for disabled children's parents
sections.summary: Children with disabilities need extra parental support, and their parents need support from community, employers and sound policies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Children with disabilities need additional support from their parents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And their parents, in turn, need support from the community, their employers and, ultimately, sound policies.

sections.label: MP urges more parental support
sections.summary: The speaker commends CDCA improvements and urges MSF to further share the parenting load for children with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am glad that the Ministry recognises that each and every child is precious and can thrive under the right environment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I commend the Government’s effort to improve upon the CDCA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is a small step towards better parental support for young Singaporeans and it benefits all children, whether they have a disability or not.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As we reflect on the Government’s proactivity towards societal changes, I urge MSF to consider this third response, to share the parenting load of children with disabilities more extensively.

sections.label: Paternity leave and maternity apportionment
sections.summary: An MP asks whether couples can still apportion up to four weeks of maternity leave so fathers get up to two months of paternity leave.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: With the increment of the Government-paid paternity leave or benefit from two to four weeks, I wish to take this opportunity to seek clarifications if couples will still be able to enjoy this flexibility of enabling the working mother to apportion up to four weeks of her maternity leave with her husband, such that her husband can have up to two months of paternity leave to support his wife and their new-born child.

sections.label: Maternity leave start date
sections.summary: Under the Bill, female employees may only start maternity leave no earlier than 28 days before childbirth.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Under the Bill, female employees may only commence their maternity leave no earlier than 28 days before childbirth.

sections.label: Flexibility for medically certified cases
sections.summary: The MP asks whether MSF would consider amendments allowing flexibility on the maternity leave commencement date for medically certified cases.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: On this note, I would like to ask whether MSF would consider additional amendments that will allow some flexibility on the commencement date of the maternity leave for those medically certified cases.

sections.label: Child Development Account and family care leave
sections.summary: The MP raises readjusting CDA restrictions for child-related expenses and cites feedback calling for family care leave.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: My third point pertains to the readjustment of Child Development Account restrictions to include other child-related expenses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: One common reply was the concern over rising inflation and increased cost of living.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: They shared that while they appreciate our local community’s effort in cushioning such impacts, they also hope that more flexibility can be exercised on how monies in the Child Development Account (CDA) can be utilised.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Although many parents still see the need to enrol their kids for these optional activities to prevent them from "losing out", doing so would require the parents to pay out of their own pocket an amount ranging from a few hundred to several thousands of dollars per month as they are not allowed to tap on their CDA funds.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In a recent focused group discussion which I co-organised in my capacity as the Head of Policy for PAP Women’s Wing, one resounding feedback gathered from over 70 participants was a consensus call for the introduction of family care leave, in order to provide some flexibility for Singaporeans to deal with various family issues that may crop up from time to time.

sections.label: Employer feedback on leave issues
sections.summary: The MP asks MSF to share employer feedback on issues faced and whether these were shared with employees.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: To this end, can MSF share, based on the feedback that they have gathered from its various engagements conducted with employers, what are some of the issues that employers have been facing, or expect to face in this regard and whether such concerns were shared with their employees so as to arrive at a win-win outcome?

sections.label: Government-paid paternity leave doubled
sections.summary: GPPL doubles from two to four weeks for fathers of Singaporean children born from 1 January 2024, with voluntary employer provision and Government reimbursement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The GPPL will be doubled from two to four weeks for fathers of Singaporean children born from 1 January 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: As a start, employers have the option to provide the extra two weeks of leave voluntarily, and the Government will reimburse them.

sections.label: Paternity leave take-up rate
sections.summary: A member notes low paternity leave take-up of 55% in 2019 and asks the Ministry for the latest take-up rate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Offering paternity leave is not sufficient in isolation, and this is reflected by the low take-up of paternity leave of 55% in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Could the Ministry share the latest take-up rate of paternity leave?

sections.label: Citibank Maternity Matters programme
sections.summary: Citibank runs a Maternity Matters programme supporting mothers with handover plans and buddy programmes for returning to work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: For example, Citibank has been running a “Maternity Matters” programme, aimed to support mothers throughout their motherhood: from providing support in designing handover plans and also buddy programmes to help mothers assimilate back into the workforce post-delivery.

sections.label: Workers caregiving for elderly
sections.summary: As the population ages, more workers will have to assume some caregiving responsibilities for their elderly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Increasingly, as our population ages, more of our workers will have to assume some caregiving responsibilities for their elderly.

sections.label: Support for elderly caregiving workers
sections.summary: A member hopes the Government will support workers caring for the elderly and recognise family members' caregiving involvement as Singapore ages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: As we work towards providing support for our workers to care for their young children, I hope that the Government can also look into providing more support for workers with caregiving responsibilities for the elderly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: As Singapore ages rapidly, I urge the Government to also consider how we may also recognise and facilitate our family members’ active involvement in the caregiving of their elderly family members.

sections.label: Extended paternity leave milestone
sections.summary: Extending paternity leave from two to four weeks in the Child Development Co-Savings Act marks a milestone in Singapore's commitment to gender equality.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The proposed extension to paternity leave from two weeks to four weeks in the Child Development Co-Savings Act marks an important milestone in Singapore’s commitment to gender equality.

sections.label: HSBC leave increases
sections.summary: At HSBC, paternity leave will rise to eight weeks from two, and maternity leave to 26 weeks from 16.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For HSBC, paternity leave will increase to eight weeks, up from the current two weeks; while maternity leave will increase to 26 weeks, up from 16 weeks.

sections.label: Caregiving as reason for not working
sections.summary: MOM's 2022 survey found about 90,300 residents outside the labour force cited caregiving as the main reason for not working, 12,400 caring for aged, ill or disabled parents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Based on the Ministry of Manpower (MOM)'s 2022 labour force survey, about 90,300 residents outside the labour force cited caregiving responsibilities as the main reason for not working, and 12,400 of these caregivers were looking after aged, ill or disabled parents.

sections.label: Call for paid eldercare leave
sections.summary: A member urges the Government to consider paid eldercare leave for all, especially the self-employed, similar to proposed paternity leave.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Anecdotally, I have heard from members of the arts community that eldercare duties can be not only isolating but a source of extreme financial stress while juggling the demands of freelance jobs that do not offer leave provisions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I know that this is not the subject of the Bill today, but I do urge the Government to consider paid eldercare leave entitlements for all and especially for the self-employed, in a similar manner to what is presently being proposed for paternity leave.

sections.label: Redefining village and parental leave
sections.summary: Shifting trends like dual-income families and smaller households require redefining "village", and parents will welcome more paid leave, especially for fathers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: However, shifting attitudes and social trends, such as dual-income families and smaller households, would need us to redefine what a "village" means in modern-day Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I believe that Singapore parents will welcome this Bill and the providence of more paid leave for parents, especially for fathers, as they heed the call for a more balanced share of child caregiving duties.

sections.label: Fathers' paternity leave uptake
sections.summary: Only 40% of eligible fathers used the full two-week Government-Paid Paternity Leave between 2018 and 2020.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: For example, merely 40% of eligible fathers made use of the complete two-week duration of Government-Paid Paternity Leave between 2018 and 2020.

sections.label: Survey on flexible work arrangements
sections.summary: An NTUC Women and Family Unit survey of 2,711 respondents found 87% said flexible work arrangements are important in deciding to stay or leave jobs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In a recent survey by the NTUC's Women and Family Unit on FWAs, 87% of 2,711 respondents, both men and women, said that FWAs are an important factor in their decision-making to stay or leave their current jobs.

sections.label: CUB programme and work redesign
sections.summary: NTUC's CUB programme piloted with a company offering flexible hours, locations and training, alongside work redesign including a new HR team and scheduling system.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: At the NTUC Women and Family Unit, we recently introduced the C U Back at Work Programme, or what we call CUB programme for short.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: This programme piloted with a Singapore-based company which provides fully flexible work hours, flexible work locations and even flexible training hours in an effort to attract and retain working parents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: This programme was launched to much fanfare and with successful return to work applicants, both mothers and fathers They shared that the programme enabled them to come back to work as the company had a work culture which not only tolerated but embraced working parents' needs for leave and flexible work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: However, in the same period of time, the company also went through, with the help of NTUC, e2i and company training committees (CTCs), a continued process of work redesign, including investing in a new HR team, a new scheduling system, a policy of recognising employees who have covered the work of co-workers on extended leave and a clear policy of career progression and performance appraisals.

sections.label: Support for family-friendly employers
sections.summary: The Government can consider supporting employers in job redesign and recognising companies that adopt family-friendly workplace policies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In the equipping of our companies in long-term adoption of FWAs, the Government can consider supporting our employers in their job redesign processes, which often can be costly and may be disruptive to current business processes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: MSF can also consider awarding companies which adopt and embrace family-friendly workplace policies a form of recognition, so that their best practices can be shared and further propagated.

sections.label: Doubling paternity and infant care leave
sections.summary: The bill seeks to double GPPL, GPPB and UICL from 1 January 2024, with Government reimbursement and voluntary company implementation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The proposed bill seeks to double Government-Paid Paternity Leave (GPPL), Government-Paid Paternity Benefit (GPPB) and Unpaid Infant Care Leave (UICL) from 1 January 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Businesses appreciate the pragmatic approach taken with GPPL enhancements, such that the Government will reimburse companies for the additional two weeks of paternity leave taken by employees and implementation by companies will be voluntary for a start.

sections.label: Economic headwinds and business costs
sections.summary: Singapore's economy faces headwinds, MTI lowered 2023 GDP growth to 1.5%, and over 85% of companies expect cost increases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Singapore's economy will continue to face strong headwinds ahead.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We narrowly avoided a technical recession in the previous quarter and the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) has reduced the upper bound of 2023's GDP growth of Singapore from 2.5% to 1.5%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Singapore Chinese Chamber of Commerce's 2023 survey also came out with similar concerns as the SBF survey, indicating that over 85% of companies expect costs to increase, with more SMEs, expecting a higher cost increase of about 10% to 25%, compared to large companies.

sections.label: Consolidated pool of skilled workers
sections.summary: Stakeholders could collaborate with frontline service sectors on a skilled worker pool for SMEs, with possible Government pilot funding.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There exists also an opportunity for essential stakeholders, including Government agencies, labour unions, trade associations and chambers, to collaborate with frontline service sectors in creating a consolidated pool of skilled workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This pool could be deployed to provide immediate workforce support for SMEs within these industries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Current job platforms facilitate ad hoc job matching but lack a structured approach to organising this workforce pool, ensuring they receive training, insurance and other forms of support for swift and effective deployment to SMEs, especially on short notice, a pressing need in regulated fields like the security industry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Government could consider providing initial funding to key players for piloting such initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Also, such an enhancement to GPPL and GPML, taken together along with initiatives such as Tripartite standards and Progressive Wage (PW) Mark accreditation are necessary for us to build a fairer and more inclusive workforce.

sections.label: McKinsey study on paternity leave
sections.summary: A McKinsey study found all fathers surveyed were glad they took paternity leave and 90% saw improved partner relationships.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: According to a McKinsey study on paternity leave, 100% of fathers surveyed expressed that they were glad that they took paternity leave and would do so again; and 90% of fathers noticed an improvement in their relationship with their partners.

sections.label: Global statutory paid paternity leave
sections.summary: Worldwide, 90 of 187 countries offer statutory paid paternity leave, with four in 10 organisations providing above-minimum paid leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: Worldwide, 90 out of 187 countries offer statutory paid paternity leave, with four in 10 organisations providing paid leave above the statutory minimum.

sections.label: Sweden and Slovenia parental leave
sections.summary: Sweden gives new parents 480 days of leave at 80% pay, while Slovenia guarantees fathers 90 days of paternity leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: In Sweden new parents are entitled to 480 days of leave at 80% of their normal pay.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: In Slovenia, fathers have a guaranteed 90 days of paternity leave, with the first 15 days at 100% while the remaining 75 are paid at minimum wage.

sections.label: Doubling of paternity leave
sections.summary: The doubling of Government-Paid Paternity Leave from two weeks to four is described as transformative.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The doubling of the Government-Paid Paternity Leave from two weeks to four is not just a commendable move; it is transformative.

sections.label: Support for SMEs
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Ministry to consider additional support measures for SMEs amid potential disruption to business operations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: And while the Government's commitment to reimburse wage costs is reassuring, the potential disruption to business operations is a valid concern.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I urge the Ministry to consider additional support measures for SMEs, perhaps in the form of temporary manpower assistance or even further training to ensure smooth business operations in such times.

sections.label: Benefits for all working parents
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Ministry to consider extending these benefits to all working parents regardless of employment nature.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: It is crucial to ensure that they, too, can benefit from these provisions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: So, I urge the Ministry to consider how these benefits can be extended to all working parents, regardless of their employment nature.

sections.label: Shared Parental Leave introduction
sections.summary: The introduction of Shared Parental Leave, allowing parents to share up to eight weeks of maternity leave, is called a progressive step.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Furthermore, the introduction of the Shared Parental Leave, allowing parents to share up to eight weeks of maternity leave, is a progressive step.

sections.label: Values and Bill's objective
sections.summary: The speaker calls for a paradigm shift in societal values and commends the Ministry for introducing the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: It is a reflection of our values, our aspirations and our commitment to our future.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: But as we move forward, let us remember that policies alone are not enough.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: We need a paradigm shift in our societal values where we prioritise holistic development and foster a strong sense of community.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: While we must address the concerns raised, they should not deter us from the primary objective of this Bill – to support and nurture Singaporean families.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I commend the Ministry for introducing this Bill and hope to see its successful implementation, ensuring a more supportive future for all Singaporeans.

sections.label: Unpaid Infant Care Leave increase
sections.summary: The Bill proposes six more days of Unpaid Infant Care Leave per parent yearly for two years, for Singaporean parents of infants under two.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Bill proposes to increase Unpaid Infant Care Leave for Singaporean parents with infants under two years old by six days per parent per year for the first two years, with amendments requiring companies to offer this additional time off to all qualified Singaporean parents who have worked for at least three months.

sections.label: Paternity leave schemes welcomed
sections.summary: The enhancement of the Government-Paid Paternity Leave and Government-Paid Paternity Benefit schemes are much welcomed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The enhancement of the Government-Paid Paternity Leave and Government-Paid Paternity Benefit schemes are much welcomed.

sections.label: SME challenges with parental leave
sections.summary: A speaker notes SMEs face challenges with additional parental leave, even unpaid leave, echoing Nominated Member of Parliament Mr Mark Lee.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   Lastly, like what Nominated Member of Parliament Mr Mark Lee mentioned yesterday, we need to be mindful of the challenges that SMEs face when dealing with additional parental leave even if it is unpaid leave.

sections.label: Reimbursing supportive SMEs
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the relevant Ministry can explore reimbursing and recognising SMEs that are supportive towards their employees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Can the relevant Ministry explore the possibility of reimbursing and recognising these SMEs which are supportive towards their employees?

sections.label: Paternity leave take-up rates
sections.summary: Take-up rates rose from about 25% in 2013 to 53% in 2021, and 97% of married survey respondents agreed paternity leave let fathers play a bigger role.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: To Mr Desmond Choo and Assoc Prof Razwana Begum's question, since the introduction of Government-Paid Paternity Leave, take-up rates have increased from about 25% in 2013 to 53% in 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: From the Marriage and Parenthood Survey 2021, 97% of the married respondents agreed that paternity leave allowed fathers to play a bigger role in their newborn's life.

sections.label: Paternity Benefit for ineligible fathers
sections.summary: Fathers not eligible for Government-Paid Paternity Leave, such as those on short-term contracts, may receive the comparable cash Government-Paid Paternity Benefit instead.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: For fathers who are not eligible for Government-Paid Paternity Leave, such as those on short-term contracts, they may receive the Government-Paid Paternity Benefit, which is a comparable cash benefit in lieu of the paternity leave.

sections.label: Private childcare sick leave survey
sections.summary: In 2020, 27% of private companies voluntarily gave employees additional paid childcare sick leave.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Based on the latest available survey data from 2020, 27% of private companies voluntarily provided additional paid childcare sick leave to employees.

sections.label: Shared Parental Leave for fathers
sections.summary: Fathers can take up to four weeks of Shared Parental Leave from the mother's Government-Paid Maternity or Adoption Leave.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Couples who wish to have the father spend more time with their newborns can have the father tap on Shared Parental Leave for up to four weeks from their wife's Government-Paid Maternity Leave or Adoption Leave.

sections.label: Foster parents leave eligibility
sections.summary: Foster parents are not eligible for Government-Paid Maternity or Paternity Leave but get childcare and Unpaid Infant Care Leave.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Hence, foster parents are not eligible for Government-Paid Maternity or Paternity Leave.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: However, they are entitled to the same quantum of childcare leave and Unpaid Infant Care Leave as biological or adoptive parents.

sections.label: Purpose of maternity leave
sections.summary: Maternity leave lets mothers recover from childbirth and care for newborns, though they may start it up to 28 days early.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The primary intent of maternity leave is to provide mothers with time to recover from childbirth and to care for their newborns.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We allow flexibility for mothers to start their maternity leave earlier, up to 28 days before delivery, but the bulk of their maternity leave should still be used for post-confinement.

sections.label: Gig workers leave benefits
sections.summary: Dr Wan Rizal said gig workers should benefit from leave provisions, which are cash benefits in lieu of Government-paid leave.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Dr Wan Rizal stated that it is crucial to ensure gig workers can also benefit from these leave provisions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: These are cash benefits granted in lieu of the Government-paid portion of paid leave.

sections.label: Voluntary paternity leave for employers
sections.summary: Two weeks of Government-Paid Paternity Leave is voluntary so employers can adjust, with mandatory status intended after consultations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Mr Don Wee, Mr Mark Lee, Mr Yip Hon Weng and Dr Wan Rizal have highlighted that companies, especially SMEs who have fewer employees, may face operational challenges, and have suggested providing additional support for them.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We have introduced the additional two weeks of Government-Paid Paternity Leave on a voluntary basis, so that employers have some time to make adjustments according to their manpower and operational needs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We intend to make this provision mandatory in due course and we will be conducting the necessary stakeholder consultations with tripartite partners before any such move.

sections.label: Progressive Wage Mark for employers
sections.summary: Companies paying lower-wage workers progressive wages can adopt the Progressive Wage Mark to profile themselves as responsible employers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Companies who pay their lower-wage workers progressive wages can also adopt the Progressive Wage Mark to profile themselves as responsible employers that support the uplifting of lower-wage workers.

sections.label: Funding for special needs families
sections.summary: The Government provides funding support and means-tested subsidies for children in early intervention programmes, SPED schools and SSCCs to keep fees affordable.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We fully recognise that families caring for children with special needs face more financial challenges.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Hence, the Government provides funding support and means-tested subsidies for children enrolled in early intervention programmes, Special Education (SPED) schools and Special Student Care Centres (SSCCs) to keep fees affordable for families with children with special needs.

sections.label: Inclusive Support Preschool pilot
sections.summary: ECDA started the Inclusive Support Preschool pilot to integrate early childhood and early intervention support for children with developmental needs in a preschool setting.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The Early Childhood Development Agency (ECDA) has also started the Inclusive Support Preschool pilot to integrate early childhood and early intervention support for children with developmental needs within a preschool setting to provide a more inclusive learning experience and reduce the need for caregivers and children to shuttle between preschools and Early Intervention (EI) centres.

sections.label: Verifying parental leave claims
sections.summary: MSF has measures to verify parental leave claims, with annual commitment for paternity leave enhancements about $57 million.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Mr Yip Hon Weng and Dr Wan Rizal have raised concerns about potential misuse of parental leave.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: These are valid concerns as the annual commitment for the enhancements to Government-Paid Paternity Leave and Government-Paid Paternity Benefit amounts to about $57 million.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: MSF has measures in place to verify the authenticity of parental leave claims.

sections.label: Approved Person suspended for records
sections.summary: In the past three years, one Approved Person was suspended due to failure to keep proper records.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: In the past three years, one Approved Person has been suspended due to their failure to keep proper records.
